To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The unified theory of acceptance of technology (UTAT) model was extended in a consumer context to study acceptance and usage of technology.

The UTAUT model is extended by adding three constructs (hedonic motivation, price-value and habit) and by including moderating effects of individual characteristics (gender, age and experience) on the effects of the constructs on intention to use and actual use of technology.

(1) hedonic motivation, habit, and perceived price value are important determinants of mobile Internet usage; (2) age, gender, experience, and habit moderate the effects of perceived price value, and hedonic motivation on mobile Internet usage; and (3) habit, gender, and perceived price-value are important determinants for mobile Internet usage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the acceptance and use of information technologies (IT) and the development of a model that explains the determinants and the dynamics of this process in the consumer context.
the acceptance and use of information technology by consumers.
the factors influencing consumer adoption and usage of technology.
